records.summary: 2127 Irving St sits in the Irving Street Neighborhood Commercial District (NCD-IRVING), where limited restaurants are principally permitted under Planning Code §732. The address had a limited restaurant (Sip Tea 1011 SF) approved in 2019 as a change of use from a prior food establishment, exempted from Section 312/311 neighborhood notice. The block is densely developed with food and drink businesses: 22 registered establishments within 500 feet and 4 active ABC Type 41 licenses within 500 feet. The site is also within the Family and Senior Housing Opportunity Special Use District, which governs housing but does not restrict restaurant uses. Too few comparable use decisions exist nearby in the last 10 years to calculate an approval rate (N=0 dated use decisions within 1,000 ft).

patterns.pattern: Formula retail food concepts on this block have not successfully completed the CUA process: two applications (Mochi Donut Shop and Krispy Krunchy Chicken) at 2126 and 2130 Irving were both cancelled in 2021–2022 without reaching a Commission hearing, while a non-formula boba shop at the subject address and independent restaurants throughout the corridor were approved as principally permitted limi…

Planning staff explicitly stated in a 2021 health referral for The Mochi Donut Shop that formula retail use is not permitted in the Irving Street NCD and that while standardized merchandise is allowed, additional standardized features (branding, decor, facade treatments) would not be permitted without CUA approval, which was never obtained.

Independent limited restaurants (cafes, boba shops, bakeries) on the Irving corridor are routinely approved by Planning staff as principally permitted uses under §732 via health department or ABC referrals, with no neighborhood notice or hearing required when there is no change in use intensity.

The only successful formula retail CUA in the Irving NCD in the past three years was a bank branch at 2257 Irving, which took 11 months (341 days) and was approved with 20 conditions including community liaison, signage program review, and operational controls.

Older cafe and fast-food approvals (1985, 1994) required CUA under the prior NC-2 zoning rules, with timelines of 41–78 days to decision. The current Irving NCD rules make limited restaurants principally permitted, so these historical cases show the discretionary review pathway but do not reflect today's baseline entitlement.

approvals.summary: Planning Code § 732 does not permit formula retail for Limited Restaurant use in the Irving Street NCD; two formula retail limited restaurant CUA applications on this block were cancelled in 2021–2022 without reaching a hearing.

findings.text: Planning Code § 732 states that formula retail is a conditional use in the Irving Street NCD but is not permitted for Limited Restaurant use in this district.

A Conditional Use Authorization for formula retail limited restaurant (The Mochi Donut Shop) at 2126 Irving St, 46 meters away, was filed November 2021 and cancelled December 2021 after 22 days; the records do not state why it was cancelled.
A second formula retail CUA (Krispy Krunchy Chicken) at 2130 Irving St, 56 meters away, was filed March 2021 and cancelled January 2022 after 314 days; the records do not state why it was cancelled.

Planning approved The Mochi Donut Shop's health permit in December 2021 with the explicit condition that formula retail use is not permitted within the Irving Street NCD and that while standardized merchandise is allowed, additional standardized features (branding, decor) would not be permitted.

Independent (non-formula retail) limited restaurants on the Irving corridor are routinely approved as principally permitted uses via health department referrals with no hearing, including the prior tenant at 2127 Irving St (Sip Tea 1011 SF), approved January 2020.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is required and is issued after plan check and inspection without a hearing; the health permit application is sent to Planning for zoning review.

findings.text: San Francisco Department of Public Health issues a health permit to operate for food facilities after plan check and a final inspection confirming the facility matches approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff.
The FY 2026–27 health permit application fee is $470 (including initial inspection) with no annual license fee for restaurants and bars through 2028; reinspections are $276 per hour.
The health permit application is referred to the Planning Department for zoning review before issuance.

approvals.summary: The rules cannot determine whether a building permit is needed because the occupancy group depends on whether the space is for fewer than 50 people, whether the business is enlarged, and the existing occupancy group, which only plans or an inspection can show.

findings.text: Under the Building Code, a restaurant or bar is Assembly Group A-2, and a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B; the description does not give the occupant load, so the proposed occupancy group is not established.

The existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records; a change of occupancy is not established without the occupant load, whether the business is enlarged, and the existing occupancy group from plans or an inspection.

A limited restaurant (Sip Tea 1011 SF) was approved at 2127 Irving St in 2019 as a change of use that was exempt from neighborhood notice; the records do not show what building work was completed or what the current occupancy certificate states.

filing_playbook.action: Request a written zoning determination from San Francisco Planning Department confirming whether formula retail for Limited Restaurant use is permitted at 2127 Irving St.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a zoning determination request describing the concept as a formula retail cafe with 11 other locations, standardized branding, signage, interior design, uniforms, menu presentation, and limited food preparation. Cite Planning Code § 732 and ask whether the concept is permitted by right, requires Conditional Use Authorization under § 303.1, or is prohibited. Reference the two cancelled formula retail CUA applications at 2126 and 2130 Irving St and the 2021 health referral for The Mochi Donut Shop stating that formula retail use is not permitted in the Irving NCD. Request a written answer before proceeding with lease negotiations.
